charge-accounts.intro: Landscapers often need materials today and an invoice their office can pay later. Charge accounts give that arrangement a proper place in the sale, with the customer, buyer and outstanding amount connected from the beginning.
explanation: A charge sale follows a different path from a cash purchase. Staff need an eligible account, the right buyer and any required purchase-order reference before putting the amount on account. Those checks help turn an informal promise into a transaction the office can understand.

The useful distinction comes after checkout. The invoice remains an amount owed until an eligible payment or credit is recorded against it. Keeping that history separate makes a later account conversation easier, especially when a contractor has several jobs and purchases underway at once.

capabilities.title: Account eligibility
capabilities.text: Check the active trade arrangement before completing a charge. An existing customer profile alone does not establish payment terms or permission to buy on credit.

capabilities.title: Buyer context
capabilities.text: Retain the person purchasing and the job or customer PO details required by the account, giving the contractor's office useful context when reviewing an invoice.

capabilities.title: Outstanding balance
capabilities.text: Keep the original charge and later settlements linked so the owner can distinguish what was purchased, what was paid and what still needs attention.

faq.q: Can every employee of a landscaping company charge purchases?
faq.a: No. The store must establish the account and its eligible buyers. Naming the company does not automatically give someone charging authority or access to the company's account administration.

faq.q: Does paying the invoice create another sale?
faq.a: The original charge records the purchase. Later settlement reduces the receivable through the account-payment workflow, which helps keep collection of an old invoice separate from new product revenue.

charge-accounts.demoQuestion: Show us a landscaper purchase that uses an authorized buyer, a customer PO and a later account payment.

credit-limit-controls.intro: A generous relationship with a good contractor still needs clear boundaries. Credit-limit controls put the account's eligibility decision into the charge workflow, helping staff handle a difficult counter conversation with a consistent process and an explanation.
explanation: A limit is useful when it applies to the account actually being charged. BloomSuite checks the relevant account context rather than treating yesterday's screen or a cashier's recollection as available credit. Currency, status and recorded balances all matter when reviewing an eligible charge.

When a purchase cannot proceed under the normal rules, the next step belongs to the store's authorized process. Staff should be able to explain the restriction without improvising a workaround, making the owner responsible for a deliberate exception rather than an accidental extension of credit.

capabilities.title: Account-specific decision
capabilities.text: Evaluate the intended account rather than applying one customer's balance or terms to another. This keeps a charge tied to its own recorded commercial arrangement.

capabilities.title: Current eligibility
capabilities.text: Use the supported online account check when preparing a charge, so a previously viewed figure is not treated as a fresh promise of available credit.

capabilities.title: Controlled exceptions
capabilities.text: Keep decisions about exceptional credit with the appropriate authority and store policy, giving the cashier a clear escalation path when the ordinary charge cannot proceed.

faq.q: Can we rely on a credit balance downloaded earlier?
faq.a: An old figure can miss payments, purchases or changes made elsewhere. Charge eligibility needs the supported current check; cached information should not become independent authority to extend more credit.

faq.q: Can a cashier bypass the limit to keep the line moving?
faq.a: Access to checkout does not mean unrestricted credit authority. Your store's configured permissions and exception process determine who can make a decision and what evidence must remain with it.

credit-limit-controls.demoQuestion: Show us how a purchase exceeding the account limit is explained to the cashier and escalated to the right person.

account-statements.intro: A contractor asking what they owe should not trigger a search through separate receipts and handwritten notes. Account statements bring the recorded account position into a view your team can review before discussing unpaid invoices and recent settlements.
explanation: Statements serve a different purpose from checkout receipts. A receipt explains a particular transaction; an account statement helps someone understand a continuing relationship across purchases, credits and payments. That broader view is useful when an office pays several garden-centre invoices together.

Accuracy depends on the underlying ledger. Before sharing a statement, check that recent collections and credits have been recorded against the intended account. A statement presents the records you have; it does not contact the customer, collect payment or settle a disputed amount by itself.

capabilities.title: Account overview
capabilities.text: Review the customer's recorded account activity together, providing a more coherent starting point than treating every invoice as an unrelated conversation at the counter.

capabilities.title: Payment context
capabilities.text: Check how recorded payments and credits affect the outstanding position before discussing what remains due, particularly when several purchases share one trade relationship.

capabilities.title: Original currency
capabilities.text: Retain the currency context of account records instead of silently treating an unknown or different currency as the same amount in your store's usual denomination.

faq.q: Is a statement the same thing as an invoice?
faq.a: An invoice records a particular amount charged. A statement provides account context across recorded activity, helping the customer and store review what remains outstanding and how later settlements were applied.

faq.q: Will generating a statement automatically email or collect it?
faq.a: No automatic collection activity is implied. Review the statement view and your store's sharing process, and confirm the recipient and account details before sending customer financial information.

account-statements.demoQuestion: Show us a statement containing several purchases, a partial payment and a credit so our office can follow the balance.

receivable-payments.intro: The sale may have happened last week, but the contractor is paying today. Receivable payments give that collection its own recorded purpose, helping your team reduce the right account balance without treating old debt as a new retail purchase.
explanation: An account payment needs to explain which obligation it settles. Retaining the customer, amount and allocation gives the office a way to follow the money when a customer pays in parts or asks why an invoice remains open after making a payment.

There are two records worth keeping distinct: the original sale and its later collection. Your close and accounting review need both, with their actual timing and tender context. Bank deposits and payment-provider settlements may still require their own reconciliation outside the account ledger.

capabilities.title: Account allocation
capabilities.text: Apply an eligible recorded payment to the intended receivable, retaining the relationship between the collection and the customer's outstanding obligation for later review.

capabilities.title: Partial settlement
capabilities.text: Keep a remaining balance understandable when an account is paid over more than one collection, rather than marking the whole relationship paid after the first amount.

capabilities.title: Collection history
capabilities.text: Preserve the original charge alongside subsequent payments and credits so an owner can investigate an account question without reconstructing it from memory or replacing previous entries.

faq.q: What if a customer pays only part of an outstanding account?
faq.a: Record the eligible payment through the supported account process and review the remaining balance. A partial collection should leave the unsettled amount visible rather than closing the entire obligation.

faq.q: Does a recorded payment prove the money has reached our bank?
faq.a: The ledger records the account action. Card processing, payout timing and bank settlement remain separate evidence, so the recorded collection should be reconciled with the applicable provider or cash records.

receivable-payments.demoQuestion: Show us a partial contractor payment and how the remaining amount appears on the next statement.

tax-exemption-evidence.intro: A familiar contractor's name is not enough to establish that every purchase qualifies for an exemption. Tax-exemption evidence helps the store retain the certificate, scope and dates behind a decision instead of relying on a permanent unchecked assumption.
explanation: The same customer can make purchases for different purposes, with products that receive different treatment. Reviewing jurisdiction, intended use and eligible product categories keeps the exemption conversation tied to the actual purchase rather than an overly broad customer label in the address book.

Documented evidence also gives the owner something useful to revisit when a certificate expires or a transaction is questioned. The software provides a structured review trail; the business remains responsible for confirming its policy and obtaining appropriate professional guidance for the jurisdictions where it trades.

capabilities.title: Certificate context
capabilities.text: Retain the supporting certificate information with its dates and scope, making it easier to see which evidence was reviewed for an eligible customer arrangement.

capabilities.title: Purchase eligibility
capabilities.text: Consider the relevant jurisdiction, product category and intended use together, rather than assuming one verified document exempts every future item the buyer chooses.

capabilities.title: Review history
capabilities.text: Keep a traceable decision behind the treatment so questions about timing, document validity or scope can be reviewed against recorded evidence instead of a cashier's recollection.

faq.q: Can we mark a landscaper permanently exempt?
faq.a: A blanket designation can overlook product, use, date and jurisdiction limits. The supported workflow reviews the evidence within its scope; your owner or adviser must confirm the actual applicable treatment.

faq.q: Does uploading a certificate mean the store can apply an exemption immediately?
faq.a: A document is supporting evidence, not automatic approval. The store must complete the relevant review and configuration, confirm validity and scope, and follow its authorized decision process before relying on that treatment.

tax-exemption-evidence.demoQuestion: Walk us through a certificate that applies to some products or uses but not every purchase on the account.

special-orders.intro: A requested specimen tree can take weeks to arrive, with several staff members involved along the way. Special orders keep the customer's request, selected items and agreed terms in one recorded arrangement that the team can return to.
explanation: This is different from an ordinary basket taken home immediately. The store may need to confirm supply, collect a deposit and arrange a later handover. Recording those pieces together helps the person answering the next phone call understand what has actually been agreed.

A special-order record should make the promise clearer without overstating it. Supplier commitment, physical arrival and customer fulfilment are separate steps. Keeping each step distinct helps your team explain progress honestly and handle a partial delivery or changed arrangement without losing the original request.

capabilities.title: Customer-linked request
capabilities.text: Connect the requested plants or products to the intended customer, giving staff an identifiable order to find when discussing progress, terms or collection arrangements.

capabilities.title: Agreed terms
capabilities.text: Retain the commercial details of the deferred arrangement so a deposit, balance or cancellation conversation has a recorded starting point beyond a note beside the till.

capabilities.title: Fulfilment progress
capabilities.text: Track what is still outstanding when the order is completed in stages, keeping later staff from assuming the entire request was handed over with the first item.

faq.q: Does creating a special order guarantee the supplier has the plant?
faq.a: No. The order records the customer's arrangement with your store. Supplier availability and commitment must be confirmed separately, and staff should distinguish a request from stock physically received and ready to hand over.

faq.q: Can we collect a deposit before the order arrives?
faq.a: The supported deferred-order workflow records eligible payments separately from completed product sales. Agree the terms first, then review how the deposit will apply at fulfilment or be handled if the arrangement changes.

special-orders.demoQuestion: Show us a specimen-tree order from customer request through deposit, supplier arrival and final collection.

customer-deposits.intro: Taking a deposit creates an obligation as well as a payment. Customer deposits help the store record money held against a future order, making the remaining balance and later application easier for both staff and the customer to understand.
explanation: A deposit should not become indistinguishable from ordinary merchandise revenue the moment it is collected. Keeping the order payment separate gives the owner a clearer account of money received before the goods have been fulfilled, especially across month-end or a long growing season.

The customer conversation starts with the terms: what the deposit secures, when the rest is due and how a cancellation is handled. The supported order workflow retains the payment relationship so the next fulfilment or correction can be reviewed against the actual agreement rather than a new guess.

capabilities.title: Order payment record
capabilities.text: Associate the amount received with the intended deferred arrangement, keeping the payment understandable even when the final goods will be collected on another day or in stages.

capabilities.title: Balance review
capabilities.text: See the recorded payments alongside the remaining order obligation, giving staff a firmer starting point when the customer asks how much is still payable before collection.

capabilities.title: Separate treatment
capabilities.text: Keep held deposits distinct from ordinary sale revenue until the supported application occurs, helping the owner and accountant review timing without double-counting the same money.

faq.q: Is a deposit automatically refundable?
faq.a: That depends on your store's agreed terms and the circumstances. Record the arrangement clearly and use the authorized cancellation or refund process; a deposit record does not decide the customer's entitlement on its own.

faq.q: How does a deposit work when only some items are collected?
faq.a: Review the eligible application during each fulfilment and retain the remaining order balance. The payment should stay connected to its original arrangement rather than being counted again as newly collected money.

customer-deposits.demoQuestion: Show us how a deposit is applied to a partially collected order without being counted as a second payment.

partial-fulfilment.intro: Customers do not always need to wait for an entire order before collecting the plants that have arrived. Partial fulfilment keeps the handed-over quantities and remaining obligations visible when a deferred arrangement is completed over more than one visit.
explanation: That distinction matters at a garden centre, where suppliers may split shipments and customers may collect items as planting work progresses. The recorded order needs to tell the next staff member which lines are finished and which still require attention, without treating the first collection as completion of everything.

Money needs the same care as quantities. Review the deposit application and remaining balance during each fulfilment so the financial position follows the goods actually handled. Physical checks still belong to staff: a recorded quantity does not confirm that a particular specimen is healthy, prepared and ready outside.

capabilities.title: Line progress
capabilities.text: Retain the fulfilled quantity against the original order line so staff can distinguish what has already been handed over from what the customer is still expecting.

capabilities.title: Outstanding work
capabilities.text: Keep the remaining items available for later review instead of replacing the original order with an informal note describing what was left behind after collection.

capabilities.title: Payment application
capabilities.text: Review the eligible deposit and balance treatment for the stage being completed, preserving the connection between held money and the customer's actual fulfilment progress.

faq.q: Can a customer collect two items now and return for the third?
faq.a: That is the purpose of partial fulfilment. Record the quantities handed over and retain the remaining line, then review any applicable payment application and collection arrangements for the later visit.

faq.q: Does an item marked received mean it has been collected?
faq.a: Receiving stock from a supplier and handing goods to a customer are different operations. Staff should confirm physical readiness and record the actual fulfilment rather than assuming a delivery completed the customer's order.

partial-fulfilment.demoQuestion: Show us an order collected across two visits, including the quantities and payment balance remaining after the first pickup.

layaway-records.intro: A customer paying in stages needs a shared understanding of the purchase, payment progress and collection terms. Layaway records put that arrangement into the deferred-order workflow so staff can follow it across shifts and customer visits.
explanation: The practical value is continuity. When a different person answers the customer's question, they can start with the recorded arrangement instead of trying to remember a colleague's promise. The selected items, eligible payments and agreed terms belong together throughout the period before final collection.

Your store still decides whether layaway is offered and under which conditions. A saved record should never substitute for a clear reservation, cancellation and refund policy. Establish the arrangement first, then use the workflow to keep the financial and fulfilment history aligned with that agreement.

capabilities.title: Recorded arrangement
capabilities.text: Keep the intended purchase and customer relationship together, providing a place to review the layaway's agreed commercial details rather than relying on a loose receipt or handwritten reference.

capabilities.title: Payment progress
capabilities.text: Retain eligible staged payments against the deferred obligation so staff can review what has already been collected and what remains before the next agreed step.

capabilities.title: Policy context
capabilities.text: Use the recorded terms when discussing a changed plan, helping an authorized manager handle cancellation or collection questions consistently with the arrangement the customer originally accepted.

faq.q: Does BloomSuite decide our layaway policy?
faq.a: No. The business must establish whether it offers layaway, what any reservation means and how payments, missed deadlines and cancellations are handled. Software records support that policy rather than creating it for the store.

faq.q: Is money received on layaway already a completed product sale?
faq.a: A payment against a deferred order is distinct from completed fulfilment. Review the supported deposit and sale application workflow with your accountant so timing and later collection are recorded appropriately for the arrangement.

layaway-records.demoQuestion: Walk us through a staged-payment arrangement, including what staff see before collection and how an authorized cancellation is handled.

rain-checks.intro: An out-of-stock conversation can still lead to a useful next step. Rain checks give the store a record of the customer's interest and agreed arrangement, without pretending that an unavailable plant is already reserved or on the way.
explanation: A rain check serves a different purpose from a completed purchase or confirmed special order. It helps the team remember a request that needs another availability conversation. Keeping that distinction clear prevents the next staff member from interpreting an expression of interest as a guaranteed supply commitment.

The strongest customer experience is an honest one. Record the relevant customer and terms, then confirm actual supply through the store's normal purchasing and stock review. If the situation changes, staff can return to the recorded request rather than relying on memory of a conversation during a busy Saturday.

capabilities.title: Customer interest
capabilities.text: Retain the request against the intended customer so an out-of-stock conversation has a findable record when the store reviews what people have been asking for.

capabilities.title: Clear promise
capabilities.text: Distinguish the rain check from a stock reservation, making it easier for staff to explain what the record does and what still needs supplier or store confirmation.

capabilities.title: Later review
capabilities.text: Return to the agreed terms when availability is discussed again, giving a colleague enough context to continue the conversation without inventing a new promise or assuming supply has arrived.

faq.q: Does a rain check reserve stock for the customer?
faq.a: No. The supported rain-check record does not reserve inventory. Staff must verify availability and establish any later order or reservation through the appropriate workflow before promising that particular goods are held.

faq.q: Should we use a rain check instead of a special order?
faq.a: Use the record that matches the actual agreement. A rain check retains interest without a stock reservation; a special order records a more specific deferred purchase arrangement with its own terms and payment considerations.

rain-checks.demoQuestion: Show us the difference between a rain check, a special order and stock that is actually reserved for fulfilment.

order-cancellations.intro: A cancelled order may still have a deposit, allocated plants or an unresolved refund attached to it. Order cancellations help the team close the arrangement deliberately, keeping the original agreement and its financial history available for review.
explanation: The job is larger than removing a row from a list. An authorized decision needs to address the remaining commitment, the applicable terms and any associated allocation or payment consequences. Recording that process makes a later question easier to answer without erasing what happened before the cancellation.

Separate the commercial decision from its eventual payment outcome. A cancelled order does not prove that a provider refund succeeded or that goods physically returned to the yard are sellable. Staff review those related operations through the relevant workflow and keep unresolved work visible until it has been addressed.

capabilities.title: Original history
capabilities.text: Retain the customer's order and its prior payments or fulfilments, giving the owner a reliable record when explaining why the arrangement changed and what remains to be resolved.

capabilities.title: Terms review
capabilities.text: Apply the store's authorized cancellation policy to the actual agreement instead of assuming every deposit, special order or partially fulfilled purchase receives the same treatment.

capabilities.title: Related outcomes
capabilities.text: Review eligible refunds, remaining allocations and physical handling separately, so closing the order does not silently assert that money moved or goods returned to a particular condition.

faq.q: Does cancelling an order automatically refund the deposit?
faq.a: A cancellation decision and a completed refund are separate outcomes. Your policy determines eligibility, authorized staff initiate the appropriate financial action, and the actual provider or ledger result must still be confirmed.

faq.q: Can we delete the order after cancellation?
faq.a: The supported approach retains the history needed to explain the arrangement, payments and later corrections. That evidence is useful if a customer questions the amount or staff need to reconcile a related transaction.

order-cancellations.demoQuestion: Show us a cancelled special order with a deposit, including how pending financial work remains distinguishable from a completed refund.

pickup-planning.intro: A collection day becomes easier when the team knows which orders belong together and how much work each pickup group represents. Pickup planning helps organize supported order batches before customers arrive expecting their plants to be ready.
explanation: The benefit appears before the first handover. Reviewing assigned orders and batch capacity gives the manager a concrete preparation list instead of a long unsorted collection of customer names. That is particularly useful for presales and fundraisers with many similar products due around the same time.

Planning is still distinct from physical readiness and fulfilment. Staff must prepare the actual goods, check what has arrived and record the handover through the appropriate order workflow. A scheduled place in a batch should never be treated as proof that every item is already assembled outside.

capabilities.title: Order grouping
capabilities.text: Build supported pickup batches around the recorded orders, making the work easier to review together when a campaign or seasonal event creates a concentrated collection period.

capabilities.title: Capacity review
capabilities.text: Consider the supported batch limits before assigning more orders, helping managers organize a workable collection plan rather than relying on an unlimited list of promised arrivals.

capabilities.title: Handover context
capabilities.text: Keep the assigned orders findable for the team carrying out collection, while retaining the distinction between an order on the plan and goods physically handed to a customer.

faq.q: Does assigning a pickup batch mean the order is ready?
faq.a: No. Batch assignment organizes the work. Staff still confirm stock, prepare the goods and complete the appropriate handover record; a place on a schedule is not evidence that the plants have arrived.

faq.q: Can pickup planning help with a fundraiser collection day?
faq.a: The supported campaign workflow includes pickup batches and assigned orders. Review the campaign, allocation and capacity configuration in your demo so the plan matches the way your team will physically handle collection.

pickup-planning.demoQuestion: Show us a busy fundraiser pickup day, including batch capacity, preparation and the distinction between scheduled and collected orders.

delivery-planning.intro: A local delivery promise contains more than an address. Delivery planning gives the owner a place to review customer orders and agreed arrangements, helping the team see the details that need confirmation before goods leave the garden centre.
explanation: This supports the store's own delivery operation rather than replacing it with an assumed shipping service. Staff need a clear view of the order, selected arrangement and relevant details so the person preparing the plants can work from the same understanding as the person arranging the delivery.

Keep planning, charging and fulfilment distinct. A configured delivery zone or recorded schedule does not collect money, optimize a route or confirm a doorstep handover. The value is a more organized operational conversation, with actual stock, fees and completion handled through their appropriate store processes.

capabilities.title: Order context
capabilities.text: Review delivery arrangements in relation to the customer's recorded purchase, helping staff connect the planned visit to the goods and outstanding work that actually belong to that order.

capabilities.title: Agreed details
capabilities.text: Keep the relevant location and timing information visible for review, making it easier to identify missing decisions before a driver or preparation team relies on the plan.

capabilities.title: Store-led execution
capabilities.text: Support the garden centre's own operational handoff while leaving physical preparation, transport and confirmation with the people carrying out the delivery under the store's usual procedures.

faq.q: Does this automatically choose the fastest delivery route?
faq.a: No route optimization is implied. The owner workspace supports recorded planning and arrangements; routing, vehicle capacity and real-world transport decisions remain part of the store's own delivery operation and any separately confirmed tools.

faq.q: Are delivery fees collected when a zone is saved?
faq.a: A planning record or configured zone is not a payment. Review the agreed fee and collect it through the supported sale or order process rather than assuming a scheduling action charged the customer.

delivery-planning.demoQuestion: Show us how a local delivery arrangement stays connected to its order without implying that scheduling collects payment or completes the delivery.

presale-campaigns.intro: A seasonal presale needs a clear offer, a sensible quantity limit and a defined selling window. Presale campaigns bring those decisions into a recorded structure so the store can review commitments before the collection or delivery period begins.
explanation: Garden centres often face a narrow seasonal opportunity: a limited shipment, a holiday product or a fundraiser with a fixed end date. Keeping the offer and its allocation rules together makes it easier to understand what has been promised and where the campaign still has room for orders.

Connected channels require deliberate setup. A campaign should not be described as sharing live capacity across a website and till until the intended connection and identities are verified. The campaign records provide a way to review the arrangement; physical supply and customer fulfilment still need their own checks.

capabilities.title: Defined offers
capabilities.text: Record the campaign's products and prices within its selling arrangement so the team can discuss the same offer instead of relying on several slightly different seasonal instructions.

capabilities.title: Selling window
capabilities.text: Set the supported campaign timing and review it before accepting commitments, keeping the sales period distinct from the later preparation, pickup or delivery period.

capabilities.title: Allocation controls
capabilities.text: Use the supported caps and recorded allocations to review the campaign's commitments, with connected website or in-store participation enabled only after its intended setup has been confirmed.

faq.q: Can a presale accept unlimited orders for a limited shipment?
faq.a: The supported campaign arrangement includes offer caps and allocation rules. Configure and verify them against the intended channels and supply plan before taking live orders; a seasonal offer should not silently promise unlimited stock.

faq.q: Does a campaign automatically connect our website to the till?
faq.a: No. Cross-product business identity, product mapping and channel setup require verification. Demonstrate the actual connection for your store before relying on a shared allocation or describing the website and register as already synchronized.

presale-campaigns.demoQuestion: Show us a capped seasonal presale, including its selling dates, recorded allocations and the setup needed for any website participation.

fundraiser-reconciliation.intro: A fundraiser total needs an explanation the store can stand behind. Fundraiser reconciliation brings recorded orders, collections, refunds and attribution into the review, helping the owner discuss a campaign result with more confidence than a single unexplained number.
explanation: Campaign activity can arrive through different channels and at different stages. Money collected is not necessarily the same as booked order value, and a refund can change the final position. Reviewing those components together helps the team identify what is complete and which obligations still need attention.

Commission deserves a clear label too. A provisional campaign calculation is a starting point for review, not proof that a partner has been paid. Connected website records, customer identity and the store's agreed campaign policy must be confirmed before treating the reconciliation as the final commercial outcome.

capabilities.title: Campaign components
capabilities.text: Review the recorded value, collections and refunds separately, helping the owner explain why the amount booked for a campaign may differ from cash received or the balance still outstanding.

capabilities.title: Attribution review
capabilities.text: Retain the relevant campaign relationship when reviewing orders and corrections, so a fundraiser conversation can refer back to the underlying records instead of an isolated spreadsheet total.

capabilities.title: Provisional commission
capabilities.text: Keep calculated commission distinguishable from an approved payout, allowing the store to reconcile cancellations, returns and the agreed basis before accepting a final amount owed to the partner.

faq.q: Is the displayed commission already a payment to the school?
faq.a: No. A provisional commission is a calculation for review, not a completed payout. Confirm the campaign records, applicable refunds and agreed commission basis before deciding what is owed and handling the actual payment.

faq.q: Will online and in-store fundraiser orders appear together automatically?
faq.a: That depends on the verified connection and campaign setup for the store. Demonstrate the actual mapped channels and retained records rather than assuming that a campaign page alone establishes complete cross-product reconciliation.

fundraiser-reconciliation.demoQuestion: Show us a fundraiser report where booked orders, collected money, refunds and provisional commission are visibly different parts of the result.

staff-pin-sign-in.intro: The next sale should belong to the person actually serving the customer. Staff PIN sign-in gives a prepared register a clear cashier identity, making a shared counter more accountable without asking the team to share one generic staff login.
explanation: A garden centre can have several people stepping behind the till during the day. Choosing the correct staff identity and following the register's sign-in process helps preserve who performed the work when the owner later reviews a transaction, refund or shift question.

The PIN is one part of access, not the entire security arrangement. Register and device binding, active membership and the appropriate store permissions still matter. Onboarding should include a normal sign-in and handover rehearsal so seasonal staff know what to do before serving a real customer.

capabilities.title: Named cashier
capabilities.text: Identify the staff member using the register so later transaction review can refer to the person who actually completed the recorded work instead of a shared generic account.

capabilities.title: Bound register
capabilities.text: Use the prepared device and register context alongside staff sign-in, helping keep a cashier session associated with the intended business location and counter setup.

capabilities.title: Clear handover
capabilities.text: Give the next staff member their own sign-in step when the register changes hands, supporting a more understandable record across breaks, lunch cover and changing shifts.

faq.q: Can everyone use the manager's PIN?
faq.a: Sharing a privileged PIN undermines the purpose of named access and approvals. Give staff their own appropriate identities and permissions, then rehearse ordinary sign-in and sensitive-action escalation under your store's access policy.

faq.q: Can a completely new cashier sign in while the internet is down?
faq.a: Do not assume that offline selling also provides new offline sign-in. Prepare devices and authenticated sessions ahead of time, and confirm the supported identity and renewal limits during your store's outage rehearsal.

staff-pin-sign-in.demoQuestion: Show us a normal cashier sign-in and handover without granting the cashier access to manager-only work.

store-scoped-roles.intro: A seasonal cashier, a department supervisor and an owner have different jobs. Store-scoped roles help make those differences explicit, giving the team access appropriate to their responsibilities rather than treating every person behind a counter as an administrator.
explanation: Location matters as well as job title. A manager working at one store should not automatically receive the same operational reach across another location. Defining roles within the intended store scope gives a growing garden-centre business a more deliberate way to organize access.

Permissions need care throughout the season. When someone changes responsibilities or leaves the business, the owner should review and revoke access while retaining the history of work already performed. An access change should not erase the evidence needed to understand earlier transactions and approvals.

capabilities.title: Job-based access
capabilities.text: Use the supported cashier, supervisor, manager and owner distinctions to align access with the work a person needs to perform, rather than granting broad control by default.

capabilities.title: Location scope
capabilities.text: Associate role authority with its intended store so a multi-location business can review who is permitted to work within each operational context and under which responsibility.

capabilities.title: Retained history
capabilities.text: Revoke or change authority without deleting the person's earlier recorded work, preserving the context needed when reviewing a past approval, transaction or operational decision later in the season.

faq.q: Can a supervisor work at only one location?
faq.a: The role model supports store scope. Review the intended locations and responsibilities when granting access, and demonstrate both the permitted work and a location the person should not be able to administer.

faq.q: What happens to history when an employee leaves?
faq.a: Removing active authority should not remove the earlier operational record. Retained identity and action evidence let the owner review past work while preventing the departed employee from continuing under an active grant.

store-scoped-roles.demoQuestion: Show us a supervisor permitted to help at one store while owner settings and another location remain outside their authority.

manager-approvals.intro: A cashier needs a clear next step when a refund or price exception exceeds their authority. Manager approvals turn that moment into a defined store process, keeping the customer conversation moving toward an accountable decision rather than an informal workaround.
explanation: Good approval controls do not assume every exception is suspicious. They recognize that some decisions deserve another person and a reason. Configured thresholds can distinguish routine work from an action that needs review, while retaining who requested the decision and who authorized it.

The explanation matters after the customer leaves too. An owner reviewing an exception should be able to see the actor, approver and relevant reason together. Rehearse the actual store policy with staff, including what happens when the required authority or offline authorization is unavailable.

capabilities.title: Configured thresholds
capabilities.text: Set the supported approval boundary for sensitive work so staff know when they can proceed directly and when the next decision belongs to a supervisor or manager.

capabilities.title: Named decision
capabilities.text: Retain both the person requesting an action and the person approving it, creating a clearer account of responsibility than a shared manager sign-in used by everyone.

capabilities.title: Recorded reason
capabilities.text: Keep the explanation with the sensitive action so a later review can understand the commercial decision rather than seeing only that a refund or adjustment happened.

faq.q: Do manager approvals mean every small exception stops checkout?
faq.a: Your configured policy determines which actions require approval and at what thresholds. The useful goal is a clear distinction between ordinary cashier authority and decisions that deserve another authorized person, rather than interrupting every routine task.

faq.q: Will approvals work during an outage?
faq.a: Some supported offline approval paths depend on previously cached, valid authorization and the configured policy. Confirm the exact supported action and device conditions in rehearsal; do not assume any manager can approve every action while disconnected.

manager-approvals.demoQuestion: Show us an above-threshold refund with its requested action, manager decision and retained reason.

action-audit-trail.intro: An owner cannot stand beside every register, stock adjustment and account conversation. The action audit trail provides a recorded explanation of sensitive work, helping the business answer who acted, what changed and which decision supported the outcome.
explanation: That context becomes valuable when a transaction is questioned days later. A price reduction with a named approver and recorded reason tells a different story from an unexplained difference. Retaining before-and-after evidence gives the review something concrete rather than asking people to reconstruct a busy shift from memory.

An audit trail records application actions; it does not observe what physically happened in the greenhouse or at the cash drawer. Use the evidence to guide a fair operational conversation, alongside the actual goods, documents and staff knowledge needed to understand the event.

capabilities.title: People and authority
capabilities.text: Review the actor and, where applicable, the approver together, showing the relationship between someone requesting work and someone authorized to permit the sensitive decision.

capabilities.title: Change context
capabilities.text: Retain the relevant before-and-after state and reason for supported actions, providing more useful evidence than a standalone timestamp saying only that something was updated.

capabilities.title: Store and device
capabilities.text: Keep operational context with the action so the owner can investigate the appropriate location, register or device rather than guessing where a recorded change originated.

faq.q: Can an audit trail prove who physically handed over cash?
faq.a: It records authenticated application actions and their retained context. That evidence supports review, but it does not independently observe physical handling or replace the store's staff supervision and cash-management procedures.

faq.q: Why keep the original record after a correction?
faq.a: A correction explains how the business addressed an earlier event. Preserving both gives the owner a coherent history, whereas replacing or deleting the first action can remove the context needed to understand the final result.

action-audit-trail.demoQuestion: Show us a corrected sensitive action where both the original decision and the later remedy remain understandable.

opening-floats.intro: A reliable close starts before the first customer arrives. Opening floats give each register session a counted starting cash amount, so the team has a common reference when reviewing sales, refunds and other cash movements at the end of the shift.
explanation: The important number is the cash actually placed in the drawer, not the amount someone remembers from yesterday. Recording the opening count helps distinguish a starting difference from a discrepancy that arose during trading, making the closing conversation more specific and less dependent on assumptions.

The software does not count the money. Staff still need a consistent physical routine and the correct register context before opening. Practising that simple sequence with seasonal employees can make the daily process easier to follow, especially when several people cover the same counter during a busy period.

capabilities.title: Counted baseline
capabilities.text: Record the actual opening amount for the prepared register session so the expected closing position begins with an explicit cash figure rather than an inherited assumption.

capabilities.title: Session context
capabilities.text: Keep the float associated with the session it starts, helping the owner review which cash baseline belongs to which period of trading and register operation.

capabilities.title: Closing foundation
capabilities.text: Use the opening record alongside sales, refunds and permitted cash movements when explaining the final difference, rather than looking at the day's sales total as the only source of cash change.

faq.q: Can we enter our usual float without counting it?
faq.a: The system can record an amount, but it cannot verify what is physically present. A real count is what makes the opening figure meaningful when staff later investigate whether a discrepancy existed before trading began.

faq.q: Is the opening float part of sales revenue?
faq.a: It is the starting cash position of the register session, not a new customer purchase. Keep its purpose distinct from sales and later cash movements when reviewing the close with your team or accountant.

opening-floats.demoQuestion: Show us how an opening float contributes to the expected cash amount at the end of a shift.

paid-in-and-paid-out.intro: Not every change in the drawer comes from a sale or a refund. Paid-in and paid-out records give permitted cash movements their own explanation, helping the closer understand why physical cash changed during the working day.
explanation: Without a recorded reason, an authorized cash movement can look like a shortage or unexplained extra money. Keeping the amount and its purpose connected gives the owner a more useful review trail, particularly when the person closing the drawer was not present when the cash moved.

This is a cash-handling control, not permission for staff to remove money whenever they choose. Your store sets the allowable purposes, supporting paperwork and approval thresholds. Rehearse the process alongside opening and closing so the team knows which movements need a record and who may authorize them.

capabilities.title: Separate movement
capabilities.text: Record eligible cash entering or leaving the drawer outside a retail transaction, keeping its purpose distinct from product revenue and customer return activity in the session.

capabilities.title: Reason and authority
capabilities.text: Retain the explanation and follow the relevant approval policy, giving a manager enough context to review why a movement was appropriate and who was permitted to perform it.

capabilities.title: Close context
capabilities.text: Include documented cash movements in the closing conversation so staff can investigate the actual expected position instead of interpreting every difference as a missing sale or refund.

faq.q: Should a petty-cash withdrawal be entered as a negative sale?
faq.a: Use the supported cash-movement process for an eligible paid-out amount under store policy. A separate record preserves why cash moved instead of inventing a merchandise transaction to make the drawer total appear correct.

faq.q: Does recording a cash movement prove it was authorized?
faq.a: The record should be considered with the configured permissions, approval evidence and store procedure. Entering a reason is useful context, but it does not replace the business's actual cash-handling authority and supporting documentation.

paid-in-and-paid-out.demoQuestion: Show us a permitted paid-out movement and how the closer distinguishes it from a customer refund.

register-assignments.intro: The device on a counter needs a more reliable identity than a sticker saying Till Two. Register assignments connect the prepared register to its intended store, helping sessions and recorded sales carry the correct operational context from the start.
explanation: This matters when a garden centre adds another lane, moves equipment or operates multiple locations. Staff should be able to confirm where they are working before opening a session, rather than letting a familiar browser or device label silently determine which store receives the day's activity.

Changing an assignment deserves deliberate handling. Saved baskets, pending payments and unsynchronized work belong to their original context and must be reviewed before a device is repurposed. Treat reassignment as a setup operation, not a convenient way to bypass an error or start a different location without checking outstanding work.

capabilities.title: Store binding
capabilities.text: Associate the register with its intended store so checkout activity begins with a defined location context rather than relying only on the physical name of a tablet or computer.

capabilities.title: Session continuity
capabilities.text: Retain the appropriate register and store identity with recorded work, making later sales and close review easier to follow across multiple lanes and different staff members.

capabilities.title: Controlled reassignment
capabilities.text: Review saved work and the supported provisioning process before changing where a register belongs, protecting the original context of activity that may still require payment or synchronization recovery.

faq.q: Can we move the same tablet to another store?
faq.a: Physical movement alone should not redefine the register. Review the supported reassignment process, outstanding work and the target store configuration before using the device for another location's sessions and customer transactions.

faq.q: Why is a named register different from a staff login?
faq.a: Staff identity explains who is performing the work. The register assignment explains the operational location and device context of that work; both matter when reviewing a sale, approval, close or recovery issue.

register-assignments.demoQuestion: Show us how a second register is assigned and what must be resolved before an existing device changes location.

multi-store-configuration.intro: A second garden centre brings more than another address. Multi-store configuration gives each location an explicit operating context, helping the owner organize stores, registers and policies without assuming every site has the same currency, timezone or legal arrangement.
explanation: The value is clarity at the boundaries. A sale should belong to the intended store; a transfer should explain where plants left and where they arrived. Configured business and location records give those operations a common foundation, rather than relying on a staff member to infer context from a device name.

Configuration should be reviewed before trading starts. Reporting currency, effective tax settings and store policies have consequences beyond the page where they are entered. A combined view does not imply automatic currency conversion or erase the need to reconcile each store's own sessions and operational records.

capabilities.title: Business structure
capabilities.text: Record the supported entity and store arrangement so the organization has an explicit foundation for its locations, registers and location-specific operational decisions within the POS.

capabilities.title: Local context
capabilities.text: Retain relevant timezone, currency and policy configuration for each store, helping the team review activity in the context where it was actually recorded and carried out.

capabilities.title: Movement between stores
capabilities.text: Support store-aware transfer records and register assignment by defining the source and destination locations clearly before plants, people or devices start working across the business.

faq.q: Does a consolidated report convert currencies automatically?
faq.a: No currency conversion should be inferred from a multi-store view. Confirm reporting currency and the supported scope, and retain original currency context rather than combining different denominations as though they were interchangeable amounts.

faq.q: Should we configure each location before adding registers?
faq.a: Yes. Confirm the business and store context first, then assign registers and appropriate staff authority to that structure. This gives later sessions, transfers and reports a clear location foundation from the beginning.

multi-store-configuration.demoQuestion: Show us two stores with their own register context and a transfer that retains both source and destination evidence.

tablet-friendly-workspaces.intro: Receiving, stock review and customer questions do not always happen beside a desktop computer. Tablet-friendly workspaces give managers a responsive way to reach supported store tasks closer to the place where they are actually working during the day.
explanation: The purpose is practical access, not simply shrinking a large table onto a smaller screen. A manager checking a delivery or reviewing a product needs readable context and an understandable next step. The same business workflow should remain recognizable as the available space and way of touching controls change.

A responsive layout is only one part of the device experience. Browser behavior, connectivity and peripherals must be checked on the equipment your store intends to use. A tablet view can support the work without certifying a scanner, printer or payment reader that has never been physically tested.

capabilities.title: Responsive access
capabilities.text: Use supported manager workflows in layouts designed to adapt to smaller screens, allowing routine review without assuming that every owner will always work from a full-size office monitor.

capabilities.title: Consistent work
capabilities.text: Keep the purpose of catalogue, receiving and operational tasks recognizable as the screen changes, helping a manager return to familiar work from an appropriate supported browser device.

capabilities.title: Device review
capabilities.text: Include the actual tablet, browser and connected equipment in onboarding so a successful page layout is assessed separately from network, printing, scanning or payment hardware behavior.

faq.q: Does a tablet-friendly layout mean every iPad peripheral works?
faq.a: No. Responsive pages and compatible hardware are different checks. The exact browser, scanner, printer, drawer and reader setup require their own review and physical rehearsal before the store relies on them during trading.

faq.q: Can the manager workspace replace a dedicated register screen?
faq.a: They serve different jobs. The manager workspace supports store administration and review; the register supports cashier work. Demonstrate the intended device and workflow together rather than assuming every screen is interchangeable at checkout.

tablet-friendly-workspaces.demoQuestion: Show us receiving and product review on the actual tablet size our managers plan to use.

guided-store-setup.intro: A good first trading day starts with knowing what still needs attention. Guided store setup brings business details, staff access, catalogue preparation and register readiness into a reviewable path before the garden centre makes promises to real customers.
explanation: Setup is more than account creation. A store can have a login and still lack an approved merchant arrangement, correct product treatment or a tested printer. Making those dependencies visible helps the owner organize the people and decisions needed for a sensible cutover rather than discovering them during the first sale.

The final step is a store rehearsal, not a filled-out form. Staff should practise ordinary sales and difficult outcomes with the intended device configuration, then confirm the commercial, provider and operating decisions that remain outside the software. Readiness means knowing which evidence is complete and which still needs a person.

capabilities.title: Business foundation
capabilities.text: Review the store identity and operating context before preparing its registers, giving catalogue, staff and payment work a consistent business and location starting point for configuration.

capabilities.title: Visible dependencies
capabilities.text: Identify the setup areas that still require action, such as merchant readiness, catalogue review or equipment checks, so missing information has a named next step rather than being quietly assumed complete.

capabilities.title: Practical rehearsal
capabilities.text: Use the prepared setup as the basis for staff and device acceptance, distinguishing completed software configuration from a real store's confirmation that it can trade under its intended procedures.

faq.q: Does finishing setup mean we can take live payments immediately?
faq.a: No. Merchant authorization, enabled provider configuration, physical equipment checks and store launch approval have separate requirements. The setup workflow helps expose readiness work rather than converting a completed form into automatic permission to trade.

faq.q: What should we practise before switching systems?
faq.a: Walk through the jobs that matter to your store, including sales, returns, receiving, uncertain payments and close. Use the intended hardware and staff, and confirm the relevant tax, guarantee and account policies before cutover.

guided-store-setup.demoQuestion: Show us the setup checklist with an intentionally missing dependency and the next action an owner should take.

sales-reporting.intro: A useful sales report helps an owner ask better questions about the day. Sales reporting brings recorded store activity into a period-based view, giving the garden centre a starting point for reviewing performance and deciding what deserves a closer look.
explanation: The first question is coverage. A report built from synchronized and projected records may not yet include work still waiting on another register. Knowing which store, period and source context a number represents is more useful than treating every attractive dashboard total as a complete picture of the business.

Revenue is one part of that picture. Tender collections, tax, deposits and reviewed margin evidence serve different purposes and should be considered through their appropriate views. Use the report to explore the recorded sales story, then follow the underlying records when an unexpected change or discrepancy needs an explanation.

capabilities.title: Store and period
capabilities.text: Review recorded activity within its intended location and reporting period, giving comparisons a defined scope instead of relying on an unqualified all-time number without context.

capabilities.title: Source awareness
capabilities.text: Consider synchronization and projection coverage when interpreting a total, so missing or delayed information is not mistaken for proof that no sales occurred during the selected period.

capabilities.title: Further investigation
capabilities.text: Use supported reporting and transaction history together when a result deserves attention, connecting the overview to the actual sales or corrections behind the question you want to answer.

faq.q: Is the sales total always the same as money deposited in the bank?
faq.a: No. Sales, tender activity, provider fees and payout timing describe different things. Review the relevant reconciliation records rather than assuming a revenue figure alone explains the amount that reached the bank account.

faq.q: What if one register has not synchronized?
faq.a: Its pending work may not be reflected in a server-based report yet. Review the register's status and report coverage before using the figure for a complete close, accounting decision or comparison with another period.

sales-reporting.demoQuestion: Show us how a sales report identifies its store, period and coverage when one register still has pending work.

cash-count-comparison.intro: Counting the drawer is most useful when the team can explain the difference. Cash-count comparison places the actual physical count beside the session's recorded expectation, giving the closer a specific amount to investigate while the day's events are still fresh.
explanation: The expectation begins with the opening float and changes through cash sales, eligible refunds and documented paid-in or paid-out movements. Reviewing those components helps the team look for a concrete cause, such as an unrecorded movement or starting difference, rather than assuming every mismatch came from a missed sale.

The count itself remains a staff responsibility. Enter what is physically present and investigate an unexpected variance through the store's procedure. Changing the count simply to match the expected amount would remove the most useful evidence the comparison is designed to preserve for the owner.

capabilities.title: Actual count
capabilities.text: Record the cash physically present at close, giving the session a measured outcome rather than replacing the count with whatever amount the software expected to find.

capabilities.title: Expected position
capabilities.text: Review the relevant opening cash and recorded movements as the basis of the comparison, helping staff understand which parts of the session may explain a difference.

capabilities.title: Variance conversation
capabilities.text: Use the discrepancy as a prompt for investigation while the people and paperwork from the shift are still available, retaining the evidence instead of silently adjusting away the question.

faq.q: Should we enter the expected amount if our first count is different?
faq.a: Enter the real count and follow your recount or review procedure. The difference is useful evidence; replacing it with the expected amount can hide the very issue the close should help the owner understand.

faq.q: Does a zero variance prove every payment is reconciled?
faq.a: It only addresses the cash comparison within its recorded scope. Card outcomes, account collections, synchronization and other financial exceptions may still need separate review even when the physical drawer matches its expected cash amount.

cash-count-comparison.demoQuestion: Show us a cash variance caused by a documented movement and how the closer traces the difference before sign-off.

end-of-day-close.intro: At the end of a demanding day, the team needs a closing routine it can follow. End-of-day close brings unresolved payment work, physical cash counting and session review into a defined finish rather than a hopeful click before everyone goes home.
explanation: A close should make outstanding questions visible. Saved or uncertain payments need their own recovery, and cash differences need an explanation grounded in the actual count and movements. Reviewing those items before completing the session gives tomorrow's staff a clearer starting point and the owner a more useful record.

Closing a register is not the same as confirming a bank payout or finalizing the accounts. It records the supported session outcome under your store's procedure. Keep the close evidence and follow the separate provider, reconciliation and accounting work required to understand the complete financial position.

capabilities.title: Open work review
capabilities.text: Identify the saved payment or operational questions that require attention before session completion, rather than treating the close action as a way to dismiss uncertain financial outcomes.

capabilities.title: Cash sign-off
capabilities.text: Bring the actual drawer count into the review so the recorded close has a physical basis and an explainable difference where expected and counted amounts do not agree.

capabilities.title: Retained session
capabilities.text: Keep an understandable outcome for the register period, giving the owner a record to revisit when a later cash, refund or trading question relates to that particular session.

faq.q: Can closing the till fix an uncertain card payment?
faq.a: No. The original payment outcome must be recovered or reconciled through its supported workflow. Closing should not invent a successful payment, erase the saved attempt or justify collecting the same customer amount again.

faq.q: Should each store use its own closing procedure?
faq.a: The software provides the session workflow, while the business confirms counting, review and sign-off responsibilities. Rehearse the routine with the people who will perform it and the actual registers, cash equipment and payment setup involved.

end-of-day-close.demoQuestion: Show us a complete close, including what happens when a payment or cash difference is still unresolved.

z-reports.intro: A closing result needs a record the owner can return to after the counter is shut. Z reports summarize the supported completed register session, helping the team review its recorded trading and cash context without relying on someone's recollection of sign-off.
explanation: Their role is specific. A Z report describes the register period that was closed, not every operational event across every store or every amount eventually deposited by a payment provider. Knowing that scope makes the report more useful when it is compared with another session or questioned later.

Use the retained summary as part of the close conversation and keep related records available for investigation. If a customer return or payment issue needs more detail, follow its underlying history. A clear closing summary should provide a useful reference, not replace the evidence behind its totals.

capabilities.title: Session summary
capabilities.text: Review the supported output for a completed register period, giving staff and owners a common reference for discussing the close after the physical counter work has finished.

capabilities.title: Defined scope
capabilities.text: Keep the report tied to its actual register session rather than assuming that one closing output represents every store, provider settlement or accounting entry in the wider business.

capabilities.title: Review reference
capabilities.text: Use the retained close context when investigating a discrepancy, then follow the relevant sale, refund or cash movement record instead of trying to reconstruct detailed events from a summary alone.

faq.q: Is a Z report our bank settlement report?
faq.a: No. A register close summarizes recorded session activity. A provider payout can include fees, different processing dates or other adjustments, so it needs separate evidence before being reconciled to a bank deposit.

faq.q: Should we rely on a Z report instead of reviewing cash differences?
faq.a: The summary complements the physical count and exception review. Investigate an unexplained difference through the closing procedure rather than treating the existence of a report as proof that every underlying transaction has been resolved.

z-reports.demoQuestion: Show us a retained Z report and the underlying records used when an owner questions one of its totals.

refund-session-reporting.intro: A refund today for a purchase last week changes today's cash or payment activity. Refund-session reporting keeps that timing understandable while preserving the connection to the original sale, helping the owner explain both the purchase history and the session that handled its return.
explanation: Those two dates answer different questions. The original sale tells staff which items, prices and tenders support the return. The refund session explains when the store actually handled the correction and which current drawer or payment review needs to account for that movement.

Keeping both relationships visible helps avoid a confusing close where an older transaction appears to have silently rewritten today's story. Review the original tender and actual refund state alongside the session information, especially when a provider outcome is still pending or a return is completed after an interruption.

capabilities.title: Original purchase
capabilities.text: Retain the sale linkage needed to understand the item, quantity and payment context that support the eligible return rather than treating the refund as an unrelated negative transaction.

capabilities.title: Current session
capabilities.text: Attribute the recorded refund activity to the session that actually performed it, helping the closer explain today's cash and tender movements even when the purchase occurred earlier.

capabilities.title: Outcome review
capabilities.text: Consider the retained refund status with its timing, so a pending or uncertain provider request is not confused with a completed financial movement merely because a return was initiated.

faq.q: Will returning an older purchase erase its original sale?
faq.a: The supported return keeps the original history and records the later correction. That relationship lets the owner understand what was sold and what was subsequently returned without rewriting the original transaction as though it never happened.

faq.q: Why can today's drawer include a refund for last week's sale?
faq.a: The cash is leaving the drawer during today's session, so the close needs that current activity. The original receipt remains relevant evidence, but its sale date does not move today's physical cash effect back into the past.

refund-session-reporting.demoQuestion: Show us a prior-day sale returned in today's session and how both dates remain understandable in the close.

tender-reconciliation.intro: Knowing what sold is different from knowing how value was collected. Tender reconciliation separates the recorded payment methods and related corrections, helping the owner compare cash, cards and account activity without assuming one blended total explains the entire day.
explanation: Each tender has its own follow-up questions. Cash needs a physical drawer comparison; a card needs its provider outcome and later settlement context; an account payment belongs to a receivable. Reviewing the components separately makes a mismatch more specific and avoids forcing unlike records into an apparently tidy number.

The recorded breakdown is a starting point for reconciliation, not a substitute for external evidence. Processing fees, payout schedules, uncertain operations and delayed synchronization can affect what the owner sees at different stages. Resolve those differences using the actual source records before describing a day as fully reconciled.

capabilities.title: Method breakdown
capabilities.text: Review the supported tender components independently so cash, card and eligible ledger activity retain their own purpose instead of disappearing into an unexplained single collection figure.

capabilities.title: Correction context
capabilities.text: Keep returns and other relevant adjustments connected to their original payment method, helping the owner distinguish a later reversal from another new sale or an unrelated cash movement.

capabilities.title: Settlement comparison
capabilities.text: Bring provider and bank evidence into the appropriate review rather than treating an internal card amount as proof that the same net amount arrived in the business's bank account.

faq.q: Why do sales and bank deposits sometimes differ?
faq.a: Revenue, tax, tenders, provider fees and payout timing describe different stages of the financial story. Compare their actual scope and source evidence rather than assuming a deposit must equal the day's displayed sales total.

faq.q: Does the tender breakdown prove all card payments succeeded?
faq.a: A recorded breakdown must be considered with actual payment states, unresolved operations and provider evidence. Do not treat an intended tender or uncertain attempt as settled money simply because it appears in a review workflow.

tender-reconciliation.demoQuestion: Show us a day with cash, card and an account collection, including why its bank deposit is a separate reconciliation question.

tax-reporting-context.intro: An owner reviewing collected tax needs to understand which transactions produced the amount. Tax reporting context retains the relevant sale treatment and supported breakdowns, giving the business and its adviser a clearer foundation for checking recorded tax activity.
explanation: Product scope, jurisdiction and the purchase circumstances can matter at a garden centre. The useful record connects the treatment to the actual sale rather than presenting an unexplained tax figure detached from the goods and decision behind it. Returns and corrections also need to retain their original context.

A report does not decide legal eligibility or submit a return simply by displaying a number. The store must confirm its configuration, evidence and professional review requirements. Use the supported records to prepare a better accounting conversation, with the relevant dates, store scope and unresolved exceptions clearly understood.

capabilities.title: Sale treatment
capabilities.text: Retain the tax context associated with recorded transaction lines so later review can refer to the actual purchase rather than applying today's assumptions retroactively to an older sale.

capabilities.title: Supported breakdown
capabilities.text: Review the available tax components within their reporting scope, giving the owner a more specific starting point than an unqualified total without store or period context.

capabilities.title: Evidence trail
capabilities.text: Consider exemption records and relevant corrections alongside the reported amounts, helping an adviser understand how treatment was supported instead of relying only on a permanent customer label.

faq.q: Does the tax report file our tax return?
faq.a: No filing or legal advice is implied by a reporting view. Confirm the applicable process with your adviser and review configuration, source coverage and exceptions before using recorded figures for a statutory submission.

faq.q: Can the system decide whether every plant is exempt?
faq.a: Product names alone are insufficient. Jurisdiction, intended use, product scope and supporting evidence may matter, so the owner must complete the relevant review and configuration rather than relying on a general gardening category.

tax-reporting-context.demoQuestion: Show us the evidence behind a taxed sale and an eligible exemption, including how a later return retains the original treatment.

owner-exception-review.intro: An owner needs to know where to look first when the day does not quite add up. Exception review highlights recorded issues such as a close mismatch or payment finding, helping the business direct attention toward questions that still need an explanation.
explanation: The value is prioritization, not an automatic verdict. A finding may point to incomplete coverage, delayed projection or an outcome that requires reconciliation. It should make the uncertainty easier to investigate without describing an unknown state as healthy or announcing that a charge failed without the evidence to support that claim.

A useful review ends with the underlying cause understood and the appropriate workflow followed. Dismissing a notification should not be confused with correcting a payment, stock position or financial record. Keep the source evidence and any required operational remedy connected to the question the owner was trying to resolve.

capabilities.title: Review-first signals
capabilities.text: Bring recorded discrepancies and incomplete sources to the owner's attention so the day can be reviewed in order of the questions that actually require a decision or further evidence.

capabilities.title: Honest uncertainty
capabilities.text: Keep unavailable information distinguishable from zero activity or a healthy result, giving the owner a more accurate picture when a source has failed or coverage remains incomplete.

capabilities.title: Source follow-through
capabilities.text: Use the relevant workspace and retained records to investigate a finding, ensuring the next action addresses its cause rather than merely removing a visible warning from the screen.

faq.q: Does a payment exception mean the customer was not charged?
faq.a: Not necessarily. It is a signal to inspect the actual retained payment and provider evidence. An uncertain outcome must be recovered before taking another payment, rather than interpreted as an automatic decline.

faq.q: Can clearing an exception fix its underlying record?
faq.a: Acknowledging a review item does not itself move money, change stock or settle a provider operation. Follow the appropriate correction or recovery process and retain the evidence that explains how the actual issue was resolved.

owner-exception-review.demoQuestion: Show us the difference between an unavailable source, an unresolved payment and a confirmed failure in the owner review.

business-data-exports.intro: Your store's records should remain useful beyond the screen where they were entered. Business data exports provide supported, authorized CSV or JSON archives, helping an owner prepare information for review while retaining the scope and context of what was exported.
explanation: An export is useful when someone needs to work with the underlying records separately: an accountant, a migration review or the owner checking operational history. Defining the business scope matters because not every archive contains every document, image or historical detail a reviewer might expect.

It is also important to distinguish access from recovery. A readable file can support review without being a complete system backup or a tested route to restore trading after a failure. Confirm the supported contents and permissions before relying on an archive for a particular business purpose.

capabilities.title: Owner access
capabilities.text: Prepare supported business records through an authorized export process, keeping access to operational information within the appropriate business and role boundaries rather than exposing unrestricted data downloads.

capabilities.title: Usable formats
capabilities.text: Work with supported CSV or JSON records for further review, giving the owner a practical way to inspect information outside the application when its documented scope fits the task.

capabilities.title: Scope clarity
capabilities.text: Review what the archive includes and excludes before handing it to another person, helping the recipient understand the source, completeness and limitations of the supplied business information.

faq.q: Is an export the same as a disaster-recovery backup?
faq.a: No. An archive may make records available for review without restoring application state, device work or provider context. Recovery requires its own tested process, including the data and authority needed to resume trading safely.

faq.q: Can we send any exported file directly to our accountant?
