faq.a: First confirm that its scope and contents suit the requested review and that sharing is authorized. Customer information, supporting evidence and file completeness deserve attention rather than assuming every export is an approved accounting handoff.

business-data-exports.demoQuestion: Show us a business archive and its contents so we can understand which review tasks it supports and what requires separate evidence.

quickbooks-close-preparation.intro: A bookkeeper needs to know what the day's money represents, not just that the drawer matched. QuickBooks close preparation organizes recorded sales, tax, tenders and liabilities for explicit review, giving the accounting conversation a clearer starting point before any supported journal action.
explanation: A deposit, gift-card issue and account collection can move value without representing another ordinary product sale. The accounting workflow keeps those distinctions visible and requires reviewed supporting evidence, including applicable costs and processor fees, rather than inventing a balancing amount to make the numbers appear complete.

The implemented journal connection is designed for the QuickBooks sandbox and still needs verified company configuration, provider authorization and accountant acceptance. Saving a review is separate from posting. The commercial promise is a more disciplined preparation workflow, not unattended production bookkeeping or a claim that every store is already connected.

capabilities.title: Source classification
capabilities.text: Review the day's recorded components according to their purpose, keeping product revenue, captured tax, tender activity and relevant liabilities from being treated as one interchangeable cash total.

capabilities.title: Reviewed mappings
capabilities.text: Prepare the supported accounting treatment using approved company and account context, with the owner and accountant responsible for the evidence and mappings appropriate to the business.

capabilities.title: Explicit journal action
capabilities.text: Keep preparation, review and any supported sandbox posting distinguishable, so a saved packet is not described as a confirmed external accounting entry before the provider outcome is verified.

faq.q: Is this an automatic live QuickBooks integration?
faq.a: No production posting should be promised from the implemented sandbox workflow. Company connection, consent, configuration and accountant review need acceptance, and a prepared or saved review is not itself a confirmed QuickBooks entry.

faq.q: Why are gift cards and customer deposits reviewed separately from sales?
faq.a: They can represent obligations or money held before ordinary merchandise revenue is recognized. The accounting workflow keeps those purposes distinct so the owner and accountant can review the actual underlying transaction rather than count every collection as another sale.

quickbooks-close-preparation.demoQuestion: Show our bookkeeper how sales, gift value, deposits and account collections are distinguished before any sandbox journal is sent.

plant-care-guidance.intro: The customer takes home a living product, and the care conversation matters after checkout. Plant care guidance gives staff a place to review available light, watering and soil information against the confirmed plant identity before presenting it as advice.
explanation: Good guidance starts with the right source. A familiar common name can cover different plants, and a universal watering interval may be inappropriate for the actual product. The supported care workflow retains source guidance and a draft-and-review process, allowing the retailer to publish the information it has checked.

This is a useful way to improve consistency without pretending every catalogue record is complete. Missing topics should remain visible as work to review. Care guidance is distinct from automated reminders or AI-generated instructions for every plant; those promises need their own source, identity and communication acceptance.

capabilities.title: Three essentials
capabilities.text: Organize available light, watering and soil guidance together, giving staff a consistent starting point for the most common care conversation when the confirmed product has reviewed information.

capabilities.title: Retailer review
capabilities.text: Keep draft advice separate from published guidance, allowing the garden centre to check plant identity and source content before making it available through the supported product workflow.

capabilities.title: Known coverage
capabilities.text: Recognize missing or incomplete guidance instead of filling gaps with invented claims, helping the team direct catalogue effort toward the products whose care information still needs attention.

faq.q: Will every product automatically get complete care instructions?
faq.a: No. Coverage depends on available source-backed guidance and retailer review. The supported workflow should preserve missing information honestly rather than invent a watering schedule, safety claim or soil requirement from the plant's name alone.

faq.q: Is this an automatic plant-care reminder service?
faq.a: Care content and ongoing customer messages are different features. Publishing guidance does not enable a reminder campaign, establish marketing permission or prove that a future follow-up journey is configured for the customer.

plant-care-guidance.demoQuestion: Show us a plant with complete reviewed care and another with missing topics so staff can see the difference.

branded-email-receipts.intro: A receipt is one of the few messages customers actively ask a store to send. Branded email receipts make that moment more useful by delivering a readable record of the purchase through the configured transactional workflow, with the store clearly identified.
explanation: The message should reflect the recorded transaction rather than act as a fresh calculation after the sale. Keeping the receipt tied to its original purchase helps the customer find the relevant details later and gives staff a consistent reference when answering a question about what was bought.

Sending also needs an honest outcome. A request entered at the till is different from a message accepted by the provider or received in an inbox. Review the store's delivery configuration and actual acceptance, and keep optional promotional communication separate from the customer's request for a receipt.

capabilities.title: Recognizable store
capabilities.text: Present the supported receipt under the retailer's configured identity, giving the customer a clearer connection between the transaction at the counter and the message they find afterward.

capabilities.title: Recorded purchase
capabilities.text: Use the retained receipt details as the basis of the transactional copy, helping the customer revisit the original purchase without relying on a staff member to recreate its amounts.

capabilities.title: Delivery workflow
capabilities.text: Retain the distinction between requesting, sending and receiving a receipt, allowing the store to investigate its configured delivery process rather than treating an entered address as proof of inbox arrival.

faq.q: Will requesting an email receipt subscribe the customer to offers?
faq.a: No. Transactional receipt delivery and optional ongoing marketing are separate choices. The store must use the appropriate preference and withdrawal process rather than infer campaign permission from a purchase or a receipt request.

faq.q: Does a successful send request guarantee the receipt reached the inbox?
faq.a: No. Provider acceptance and recipient delivery are different stages, and inbox placement can have further limits. Confirm actual delivery behavior for the configured sender and use the available status evidence when investigating a missing message.

branded-email-receipts.demoQuestion: Show us a branded receipt and how a requested copy, provider acceptance and actual delivery are distinguished.

hosted-receipt-viewing.intro: Customers need an easy way to revisit a purchase without asking staff to explain an email attachment. Hosted receipt viewing provides a signed destination for the supported recorded receipt, giving the message's view link a useful place to open.
explanation: The destination should explain the original transaction clearly. It is a receipt view, not an editable order form or a current account balance that changes the meaning of what was purchased. Retaining that purpose helps the customer and store use the same reference when discussing the sale later.

The link also deserves appropriate handling. A signed receipt destination is intended for the person who needs that transaction, not a publicly advertised customer record. Use the valid generated link and confirm service configuration rather than copying private receipt URLs into public marketing material or unrelated customer communications.

capabilities.title: Readable destination
capabilities.text: Open the supported recorded receipt in a dedicated view, giving customers an accessible way to revisit the purchase details from the transactional message that delivered their copy.

capabilities.title: Purchase reference
capabilities.text: Keep the destination connected to the original receipt so later customer service can begin with the same transaction rather than a manually reconstructed summary of the sale.

capabilities.title: Signed access
capabilities.text: Use the generated signed link for the intended receipt, treating it as a private customer-service destination rather than an ordinary public page that staff should share indiscriminately.

faq.q: Does the customer need to find the receipt in a public directory?
faq.a: No public receipt directory is implied. The supported workflow uses a signed link associated with the intended transaction, so the customer should use the valid destination supplied through the store's receipt process.

faq.q: Can we post a real receipt link as a website example?
faq.a: Keep real customer receipt links private. Use a clearly prepared demonstration example for marketing, and verify that any displayed purchase information is appropriate to share rather than exposing an actual transaction's signed destination.

hosted-receipt-viewing.demoQuestion: Show us the hosted receipt from a demonstration sale and how the view stays tied to that original purchase.

receipt-care-notes.intro: The care advice shared at the counter can be easy to forget by the time a customer reaches home. Receipt care notes bring eligible published guidance closer to the purchase, helping the shopper revisit useful information alongside the record they already requested.
explanation: This feature depends on the care content behind the item. The supported receipt rendering can include available reviewed notes, but it should not turn an incomplete product record into apparently complete advice. A customer with several plants needs guidance associated with the correct purchased products, not a generic growing tip presented as universal.

Care on a receipt is also different from an ongoing message programme. The receipt remains a transactional reference for the purchase. Reminder schedules, future promotional tips and complete public care-guide coverage require separate configuration and acceptance rather than being implied by the presence of a few useful notes.

capabilities.title: Purchase connection
capabilities.text: Keep eligible care information associated with the purchased item in the supported receipt content, giving the customer useful context when several different products came home in one visit.

capabilities.title: Reviewed guidance
capabilities.text: Use published care from the confirmed product record instead of generating an unsupported instruction during receipt preparation, preserving the retailer's role in checking advice before it is shared.

capabilities.title: Clear limits
capabilities.text: Distinguish available notes from a promise that every item has complete guidance or that the customer has enrolled in an ongoing reminder journey after receiving the receipt.

faq.q: What happens when a purchased plant has no reviewed care?
faq.a: The workflow should include only the guidance actually available and eligible for the receipt. Missing advice should not be filled with invented instructions simply to make every purchased line look equally complete.

faq.q: Will the customer receive automatic watering reminders afterward?
faq.a: Receipt notes do not by themselves enable recurring care messages. Any future follow-up journey needs its own supported configuration, appropriate customer choice and verified delivery process, rather than inheriting permission from the receipt request.

receipt-care-notes.demoQuestion: Show us a mixed basket where one plant has reviewed care and another does not, without inventing advice for the missing record.

separate-marketing-consent.intro: A customer can want proof of purchase without wanting future promotions. Separate marketing consent keeps those choices understandable at the till, helping the store ask clearly for optional ongoing communication while still handling the transactional receipt the customer requested.
explanation: The distinction is practical as well as respectful. An email address entered for a receipt identifies where that document should go; it does not explain which future offers the person agreed to receive. Keeping the preference separate gives staff a simpler conversation and the business a clearer record of the customer's actual choice.

The store still needs to configure wording that describes its real communications and an appropriate withdrawal mechanism. A software checkbox is not a complete legal compliance programme. Review the supported consent authority and connected systems before assuming that a preference automatically controls every channel or campaign in the wider business.

capabilities.title: Distinct choices
capabilities.text: Present receipt delivery separately from the optional ongoing communication preference, allowing a customer to request the transaction record without being forced to accept future promotional contact.

capabilities.title: Clear explanation
capabilities.text: Use store-specific wording that describes the communications actually being offered, helping staff explain what the optional choice means instead of treating a vague permission label as sufficient context.

capabilities.title: Connected responsibility
capabilities.text: Review which system retains and applies the preference for the configured business, especially before describing a POS choice as synchronized automatically across website, CRM and every campaign channel.

faq.q: Can someone receive a receipt while declining marketing?
faq.a: Yes. The receipt request and optional ongoing preference should remain separate. Staff should be able to complete the transactional request without interpreting the customer's purchase or address as agreement to future offers.

faq.q: Does selecting a preference make every connected campaign compliant?
faq.a: No. The store must confirm its wording, authority, withdrawal process and actual channel behavior. A recorded choice is useful evidence, but it does not prove that every external system or future communication is configured appropriately.

separate-marketing-consent.demoQuestion: Show us a customer requesting a receipt and declining marketing, including which system retains that exact choice.

bloom-pos-assistant.intro: A manager should be able to ask for help in the language of the job. The Bloom POS assistant connects supported store questions and how-to guidance with cited sources, giving the owner a starting point and a way to inspect the basis of an answer.
explanation: The useful experience goes beyond a confident paragraph. Staff can follow relevant records or maintained guides and use supported reviewed task workflows where available. The manager remains responsible for checking the suggestion and confirming an intended change; a conversation should not silently become a financial or stock operation.

Keep the boundaries of the actual source clear. Missing records are not zero activity, and an assistant response is not independent evidence that a provider payment completed. The strongest role for Bloom is to help a manager understand the work, identify a next step and review it before acting.

capabilities.title: Cited answers
capabilities.text: Ask supported questions and inspect the referenced store records or guides, making the explanation easier to assess than an answer that offers no way to see where its details came from.

capabilities.title: Contextual direction
capabilities.text: Get a starting point for the relevant workspace or store task, helping a manager move from a broad question toward the actual record or procedure that needs attention.

capabilities.title: Reviewed tasks
capabilities.text: Use the supported proposal and confirmation process for eligible catalogue work, keeping the manager involved in the intended change rather than treating conversational suggestions as permission for autonomous action.

faq.q: Can Bloom issue refunds or change stock automatically?
faq.a: No autonomous financial or stock authority should be implied. Payments, refunds, permissions and inventory changes remain in their appropriate reviewed workflows; the assistant's role and any supported task must stay within explicit authorization and confirmation boundaries.

faq.q: Is Bloom limited to a static help article search?
faq.a: The supported experience includes cited guidance and store-context questions, with eligible reviewed task assistance. Available sources and configuration matter, so demonstrate a relevant question and its citations rather than promising unrestricted answers about every aspect of the business.

bloom-pos-assistant.demoQuestion: Show us a receiving question, its cited guidance and one supported catalogue task that requires our explicit confirmation.

searchable-pos-guidebook.intro: Staff should not need to remember an internal screen name to find a useful explanation. The searchable POS guidebook organizes maintained workflow guidance, helping managers return to the right procedure when an unfamiliar task or occasional problem interrupts the day.
explanation: Some store jobs happen too infrequently to become second nature. A first seasonal order, an interrupted return or an unusual close question can send someone looking for the same instructions again. A findable guide library gives those questions a more consistent starting point than a colleague's partial recollection.

Guidance still has a defined purpose. It explains supported workflows; it does not approve a store policy, certify a physical printer or confirm a particular transaction succeeded. Use the guide as part of onboarding and everyday help, then demonstrate the actual task with the permissions and setup your store will use.

capabilities.title: Searchable instructions
capabilities.text: Find maintained guidance using the job or problem being discussed, helping a manager locate a relevant procedure without already knowing which application module or technical term owns it.

capabilities.title: Repeatable learning
capabilities.text: Return to the same supported explanation for an occasional workflow, giving staff a more consistent reference when a task has not been performed since the previous season.

capabilities.title: Assisted help
capabilities.text: Use supported cited how-to answers alongside the guide library where configured, keeping the underlying instructions available for inspection rather than asking staff to accept an untraceable conversational summary.

faq.q: Does using the guidebook mean staff do not need training?
faq.a: No. Written guidance supports learning but cannot prove that someone can complete the store's real process independently. Rehearse the common jobs with actual staff, devices and policies, then use the guides for reinforcement and occasional questions.

faq.q: Can a guide confirm that an uncertain payment completed?
faq.a: No. Instructions explain what to do; actual retained payment and provider evidence establish the outcome. Follow the relevant recovery workflow rather than treating an article or assistant explanation as proof that money moved.

searchable-pos-guidebook.demoQuestion: Show us how a manager finds receiving guidance without knowing the exact screen name in advance.

bloomsites-product-photo-sharing.intro: Choosing a better product photo should not always mean uploading it twice. BloomSites product-photo sharing gives explicitly connected, matched products a controlled route from the manager's POS gallery to the corresponding website gallery, with delivery status the owner can understand.
explanation: The important distinction is between saving locally and confirming the website accepted the change. A POS save or upload alone should not be labelled as a completed website update. The supported connection retains pending delivery and exact confirmation, making it easier to see where the photo currently stands.

This is a deliberately narrow connection. The intended business, website and product mappings must be verified before enabling it. Photo sharing does not establish universal shared sign-in, customer consent, live stock or price synchronization; those are different data relationships with their own authority and acceptance requirements.

capabilities.title: Retailer photo choice
capabilities.text: Preserve the manager's selected gallery for the matched product rather than letting a later supplier refresh silently replace the retailer's preferred presentation in the connected photo workflow.

capabilities.title: Delivery visibility
capabilities.text: Distinguish a saved local gallery from a queued change and a confirmed website receipt, giving the owner a meaningful status instead of a success message based only on upload completion.

capabilities.title: Explicit mapping
capabilities.text: Limit publication to the approved POS product and destination website relationship, keeping a photo connection from becoming assumed authority to change unrelated products or another business's catalogue.

faq.q: Does changing a photo also synchronize price and inventory?
faq.a: No. This connection publishes the approved gallery for explicitly mapped products. Product identity, pricing, stock, customers and consent have separate authority requirements and should not be described as connected merely because a photo was delivered successfully.

faq.q: Why can a saved photo still be waiting to share?
faq.a: The local edit and the website's durable acceptance are separate stages. Review the configured connection and delivery status; a successful POS save does not prove the corresponding website product already received the intended gallery.

bloomsites-product-photo-sharing.demoQuestion: Show us a local photo change, its pending delivery state and the exact confirmation from the matched website product.

reviewed-migration.intro: Switching POS systems should begin with understanding the records your store actually has. Reviewed migration brings supported source adapters, dry-run checks and control totals into the preparation, helping the owner make an informed cutover decision instead of trusting an unchecked import.
explanation: Different record types deserve different questions. A product name and price are not opening stock, while a customer list is not a verified gift-card or trade-account balance. Reviewing scope separately prevents an apparently successful catalogue import from being mistaken for a complete migration of every operational and financial obligation.

Use real exports and reconcile the agreed totals with the people responsible for the old and new systems. Supported adapters and source formats vary. The goal is a traceable, reviewed transition plan, with unresolved records visible before they become a counter problem or a customer balance dispute.

capabilities.title: Source review
capabilities.text: Check the actual available export and supported adapter before promising what can move, keeping the migration plan grounded in the store's records rather than a generic list of incumbent systems.

capabilities.title: Dry-run evidence
capabilities.text: Review proposed records and validation findings before application, giving the owner a chance to understand exceptions and confirm the intended source instead of accepting an unchecked file blindly.

capabilities.title: Control totals
capabilities.text: Compare the agreed product and balance scope with reconciled source figures, retaining explicit sign-off where required rather than interpreting a successful import action as proof of a complete business cutover.

faq.q: Can we migrate every historical sale from any POS?
faq.a: No universal history migration is promised. Supported adapters, record types and available source evidence vary, so review the actual exports and agreed scope before deciding which history and balances can be transferred reliably.

faq.q: Why is a product import different from opening stock?
faq.a: A catalogue describes what the store sells. Opening stock describes physical quantities at cutover and needs its own reconciliation. Successful name and price import does not independently verify how many healthy, available plants are actually on site.

reviewed-migration.demoQuestion: Show us a dry run with a deliberate source problem and explain which data types are included in our proposed migration.

hardware-compatibility-review.intro: Keeping useful equipment can make a POS transition more practical, but compatibility deserves evidence. A hardware review starts with the devices your garden centre already owns and checks the complete checkout arrangement before recommending what to retain, configure or replace.
explanation: A browser-based register is only one piece of the counter. Scanners, printers, cash drawers and payment readers use different protocols and have regional or model-specific requirements. An attractive page on an iPad does not demonstrate a physical print, a drawer opening or an approved Canadian card transaction.

Review the intended bundle as a working lane. Reconnection, power or internet interruptions and payment recovery need attention alongside an ordinary sale. The right promise is a careful compatibility process, followed by an actual hardware rehearsal, rather than a claim that every pre-existing device will work simply because it turns on.

capabilities.title: Existing equipment
capabilities.text: Start with the exact tablet or computer and peripherals already in the store, helping the business make a realistic reuse decision before spending on replacement counter hardware.

capabilities.title: Complete lane
capabilities.text: Assess the register, scanner, printer, drawer and reader together, because individually plausible devices still need a compatible working path when a customer is standing at the counter.

capabilities.title: Physical rehearsal
capabilities.text: Verify real scanning, printing, drawer behavior and payment outcomes on the intended models, keeping a simulated software pass separate from evidence gathered on the store's actual equipment.

faq.q: Can we run BloomSuite on a Clover terminal we already own?
faq.a: Do not assume a proprietary terminal accepts another POS application. Review the exact device and platform restrictions; an existing iPad or supported browser device has a different compatibility question from a locked payment-and-register appliance.

faq.q: Does a reader from another country work with our Canadian account?
faq.a: Do not assume readers and merchant regions are interchangeable. Confirm the account, reader country, Terminal Location and supported integration together before purchasing or attempting activation, and verify the intended Canadian payment flows on physical equipment.

hardware-compatibility-review.demoQuestion: Review our current scanner, printer, drawer and tablet together, then identify the physical tests required before we can rely on them.

offline-cash-selling.intro: An internet interruption should lead to a known store procedure, not a guessing game at the counter. Offline cash selling supports eligible local register work on a prepared device, helping the team continue under its configured rules while keeping saved and synchronized states distinguishable.
explanation: Preparation is essential. The register needs the appropriate downloaded catalogue, authenticated context and current eligible rules before the connection disappears. Offline operation does not make unavailable data current, authorize every tender or create new staff sign-in capability simply because the screen remains open.

Device-loss protection is another separate question. A sale saved on one tablet still has only one copy until the configured independent hub confirms its snapshot. Rehearse the actual cash, receipt, backup and reconnection sequence with staff so they understand which work is retained locally and which has confirmed protection.

capabilities.title: Prepared register
capabilities.text: Use supported cached catalogue and session context already available to the intended device, giving eligible cash work a defined basis rather than assuming an unprepared browser can begin trading offline.

capabilities.title: Local continuity
capabilities.text: Retain supported cash-sale work through the register's local process, keeping the customer's payment and saved operation understandable while the normal server synchronization path is interrupted.

capabilities.title: Recovery awareness
capabilities.text: Review pending work and required second-copy confirmation during the store's outage routine, distinguishing local saving, hub protection and later cloud acceptance instead of treating them as one identical success.

faq.q: Does offline cash selling include offline card payments?
faq.a: No. Offline card acceptance is not included in this promise, particularly on iPad Safari. Card, reward and other online-authorized flows have their own provider and balance requirements, even while eligible cash work can use the prepared register.

faq.q: Can we clear Safari storage if the register seems stuck?
faq.a: Do not clear site data or replace the device while work remains unsynchronized or a payment is unresolved. Follow the supported recovery procedure so the original saved events and operation identities remain available for reconciliation.

offline-cash-selling.demoQuestion: Take the prepared register offline and show us exactly when the cash sale is saved, protected by a second copy and accepted by the server.

offline-catalogue-access.intro: A plant lookup should not become impossible simply because an online request is unavailable. Offline catalogue access keeps previously downloaded product details available to a prepared register, giving staff a reference for eligible work during a connection interruption.
explanation: The useful boundary is the downloaded snapshot. Staff can work with the records the device already has, rather than expecting newly added products or later edits to appear without a connection. This helps the team understand why the local view can remain usable while still needing a refresh when connectivity returns.

Catalogue access is not a promise that every related operation works offline. Recorded stock can have freshness limits, and some prices, identity checks or payment methods require current online authority. Rehearse those differences so staff know when they can use a downloaded product and when another action must wait or be escalated.

capabilities.title: Downloaded details
capabilities.text: Keep supported product information from the prepared register's cached catalogue within reach, giving staff a local starting point for finding the correct item when the normal request path is interrupted.

capabilities.title: Known snapshot
capabilities.text: Recognize that the device is using previously downloaded records, helping the team avoid treating an older product list or price context as a real-time update from another store or channel.

capabilities.title: Clear boundaries
capabilities.text: Distinguish access to product details from authority to complete a particular sale or tender, keeping online-only checks and configuration requirements explicit even when browsing itself remains available.

faq.q: Will a product added during the outage appear on another disconnected till?
faq.a: Not until that till receives the relevant update through the supported refresh path. Offline access uses the records already downloaded to that device rather than creating a live connection between disconnected registers.

faq.q: Does seeing a cached item mean its stock quantity is guaranteed?
faq.a: No. A product record and a verified physical quantity answer different questions. Other sales, reservations and shrink may affect availability, so staff must consider recorded freshness and actual stock rather than interpreting catalogue visibility as a guarantee.

offline-catalogue-access.demoQuestion: Show us what remains available in the catalogue during an outage and which subsequent actions still require an online check.

visible-synchronization-status.intro: Staff need to know what the register has saved and what the server has actually accepted. Visible synchronization status makes pending and failed work a reviewable part of the day, helping the owner avoid assuming that a locally finished task is already reflected everywhere.
explanation: That distinction matters when reviewing reports or recovering from an outage. A queue can explain why a server-based total is incomplete, while a failed event may need more than another blind attempt. The retained work should remain available with its original identity until the supported process confirms the outcome or identifies the required correction.

Good status information changes the next action. The team can reconnect, inspect a problem or seek authorized help while preserving the saved evidence. Clearing browser storage to remove a warning would discard the very context needed to understand whether the work was accepted and how it should be recovered.

capabilities.title: Pending visibility
capabilities.text: See work still awaiting the normal synchronization outcome, giving staff a reason to check coverage before assuming a server report includes every transaction saved on the register.

capabilities.title: Failure distinction
capabilities.text: Keep failed or rejected work distinguishable from completed acceptance, helping the owner investigate the actual cause rather than interpreting every queue item as a harmless delay.

capabilities.title: Original evidence
capabilities.text: Retain saved operations and their identities through recovery, allowing the supported retry and reconciliation process to address the same work instead of creating a duplicate transaction to replace an uncertain one.

faq.q: Does an empty-looking screen prove all work reached the server?
faq.a: Use the supported acknowledgement and status evidence rather than visual assumptions. Local completion, a queued request and server acceptance are separate states, and a report may still need its own coverage review.

faq.q: Should staff create the sale again if it remains pending?
faq.a: Do not duplicate the transaction merely because its acknowledgement is delayed. Preserve the original saved work and follow recovery or authorized reconciliation so the same customer payment is not turned into a second independent sale.

visible-synchronization-status.demoQuestion: Show us a saved operation with a delayed response and how it is recovered without creating a second sale.

local-backup-hub-readiness.intro: A register that keeps working without internet still needs a plan for losing the device itself. Local backup hub readiness addresses that different problem, using an independent store-network second copy whose acknowledgement means more than a save on the original tablet.
explanation: The distinction is physical as well as technical. The recovery service belongs on a separate, persistent machine on the store network, not another tab on the same iPad. Its confirmed snapshot protects the work included in that copy; newer unacknowledged changes must remain visible as additional exposure.

A replacement rehearsal completes the picture. The owner needs the recovery credentials, trusted network setup and supported reconciliation process before relying on a recovery promise. Internet is currently required for replacement authority and reconciliation, and no software test alone establishes a timed recovery on the store's actual equipment.

capabilities.title: Independent copy
capabilities.text: Use the configured hub on a separate persistent store-network host, keeping the recovery copy outside the tablet whose loss or failure the arrangement is intended to address.

capabilities.title: Confirmed snapshot
capabilities.text: Distinguish an acknowledged durable backup generation from a local save or attempted network send, making it clearer which work has actually reached the second-copy boundary.

capabilities.title: Rehearsed replacement
capabilities.text: Review the owner recovery process and retained uncertain operations on the intended equipment, ensuring the store knows the credentials, evidence and reconciliation steps needed before a replacement register can resume safely.

faq.q: Can another browser tab on the same iPad be our backup hub?
faq.a: No. The supported protection depends on an independent persistent store-network host. Another tab on the same device does not protect against losing that device, and a second iPad is not assumed to be a supported replica host.

faq.q: Does this guarantee recovery from every kind of loss?
faq.a: No. Unacknowledged changes, lost recovery credentials and wider loss of both source and hub have different limits. Confirm the actual scope and physically rehearse replacement rather than treating the presence of a backup setting as universal protection.

local-backup-hub-readiness.demoQuestion: Show us the difference between locally saved work and a confirmed second copy, then walk through an actual replacement-device rehearsal.

plant-and-shelf-labels.intro: The product record becomes more useful when it reaches the label customers and cashiers actually see. Plant and shelf labels bring supported botanical names, pot sizes, prices and barcode data into a reviewed design that can start from the catalogue, receiving or price-change work.
explanation: Label preparation benefits from context. A receipt batch should refer to the actual accepted variant, including a reviewed substitution, rather than copying the original requested item onto whatever arrived. Copies also need an explicit decision because supplier packs and fractional quantities do not automatically equal the number of tags required.

The software supports label layout and ZPL preparation; physical output remains a separate acceptance step. The printer, resolution, ribbon, media and barcode scan must be checked together. A neat browser preview can help review text placement without proving that the final tag is durable outdoors or readable at checkout.

capabilities.title: Purposeful formats
capabilities.text: Prepare the supported plant-tag or shelf-label layout with the relevant product details, giving staff an organized design review rather than rebuilding the same information in an unrelated label tool.

capabilities.title: Workflow entry
capabilities.text: Start eligible batches from catalogue, received variants or changed prices, keeping the label choice connected to the actual operational record that created the need to print.

capabilities.title: Barcode review
capabilities.text: Carry recorded Code 128 data into the supported printer workflow while treating the browser's barcode area as a preview placeholder, not evidence that physical scanning has already passed.

faq.q: Can we print labels automatically for every quantity on a delivery?
faq.a: Copies need explicit review. A supplier pack, partial quantity or damaged receipt does not automatically equal a tag count, and the batch should use accepted actual variants rather than label goods that were not received or are quarantined.

faq.q: Does the on-screen barcode prove our printer will produce a readable tag?
faq.a: No. The printer generates the physical barcode from the prepared data. Verify the exact resolution, media, alignment and scanner with real sample output before relying on the tag format during store trading.

plant-and-shelf-labels.demoQuestion: Show us a label batch from a substituted delivery item and the physical sample checks needed before using its barcode at checkout.

network-label-printing-from-ipad.intro: An iPad can help prepare labels near the delivery, but it needs the right printing route. Network label printing uses the configured store-network bridge to reach a compatible printer, giving tablet users a supported path without pretending Safari can open a raw printer connection.
explanation: The bridge and printer form part of the store's equipment setup. Trusted local HTTPS, the intended browser origin, the selected printer and appropriate credentials need configuration together. A successful catalogue page on the tablet does not establish that the local network, certificate or physical label output is ready.

Recovery is part of printing too. The supported workflow retains a submitted batch and its job identity so an uncertain response is not silently converted into another automatic print. Staff can inspect status and physical output before deliberately preparing another batch, understanding that sent bytes and paper verified are different outcomes.

capabilities.title: Tablet preparation
capabilities.text: Create the supported label batch from the manager workflow on an appropriate device, keeping product and price review close to the receiving or catalogue task that needs the labels.

capabilities.title: Network bridge
capabilities.text: Use the configured private-store printing service for the compatible printer path, instead of assuming arbitrary Bluetooth devices or unsupported Safari connection methods can receive the prepared label commands.

capabilities.title: Saved-job review
capabilities.text: Inspect the retained job status after an uncertain response without automatically printing again, giving staff a chance to check the printer and queue before intentionally preparing a new batch.

faq.q: Can the iPad print to any Bluetooth label printer?
faq.a: No universal Bluetooth compatibility is implied. The supported ZPL route uses a configured network bridge and compatible printer, with browser trust, local access, media and physical output verified on the intended store equipment.

faq.q: What should staff do after a print request times out?
faq.a: Keep the saved batch and check the supported job status and physical printer before creating another batch. An uncertain response is not proof that nothing printed, so automatic repeated submission could produce unwanted duplicates.

network-label-printing-from-ipad.demoQuestion: Show us an interrupted iPad print request and the read-only job check staff use before deciding whether another batch is needed.

plant-guarantee-claims.intro: A failed plant can be an emotional customer conversation as well as a financial decision. Plant guarantee claims keep the original purchase, applicable promise and reviewed evidence together, helping the garden centre respond consistently without reducing the decision to an unexplained refund or replacement.
explanation: The promise made at purchase matters. New supported sales can retain the downloaded published guarantee version, while older receipts may need manual evidence review. A later policy change should not quietly rewrite what the store originally offered the customer when the plant was bought.

Human judgement remains central. Ownership, condition, timing, eligible quantity and previous remedies need review before a supported credit or replacement is fulfilled. Keeping those decisions connected helps prevent the same quantity being compensated repeatedly and keeps failed original plants from being returned to healthy sellable stock by mistake.

capabilities.title: Original promise
capabilities.text: Retain the applicable guarantee terms with supported new sale records, giving the claim conversation a reference to what was offered then rather than automatically applying today's different policy.

capabilities.title: Evidence review
capabilities.text: Connect the exact receipt line, quantity and relevant condition information to the claim, allowing the owner to consider eligibility with context instead of treating a repeated name or general complaint as sufficient proof.

capabilities.title: Verified remedy
capabilities.text: Use the supported credit or replacement fulfilment process after review, retaining the original decision and any later compensating correction rather than erasing a mistaken remedy from the history.

faq.q: Does an eligible-looking claim automatically issue a refund?
faq.a: No. Claims require human review, and a decision is distinct from completing its financial or stock remedy. Provider refunds, store credit and replacement fulfilment follow their own supported workflows and actual confirmed outcomes.

faq.q: Do we put a dead returned plant back into available stock?
faq.a: No. The failed original does not become healthy sellable inventory simply because a guarantee is accepted. Review the appropriate disposition and any actual replacement handover separately, preserving both condition and quantity evidence.

loyalty-rewards.intro: Repeat customers deserve a reward balance the store can explain. Loyalty rewards connect supported earning, redemption and return behavior to reviewed policy terms and eligible customer purchases, helping the garden centre build a programme with a traceable history rather than an informal points total.
explanation: A saved proposal is only the beginning. The manager activates the reviewed policy and records customer agreement before eligible new purchases earn under that arrangement. Historical or unattributed entries should not become spendable simply because they resemble the right customer or appear in an imported reward history.

The return journey matters as much as earning. Supported redemptions retain their original customer account, currency and allocations so returns do not silently convert reward value into cash or restart an expiry clock. Provider, balance and policy setup still require review before offering the programme in a real store.

capabilities.title: Reviewed programme
capabilities.text: Distinguish a policy proposal from activation and customer enrollment, giving the owner control over which terms actually apply before the supported programme starts awarding new eligible purchases.

capabilities.title: Purchase attribution
capabilities.text: Connect verified earnings to eligible completed sale lines and their original policy context, helping the business explain the balance instead of trusting a manually supplied subtotal or unverified historical entry.

capabilities.title: Original-tender returns
capabilities.text: Retain the original reward account and allocation during supported corrections, so a reward-funded return restores the appropriate value rather than treating it as an unrelated cash refund or a new earning purchase.

faq.q: Does every purchase earn rewards automatically?
faq.a: Eligibility depends on the activated policy, enrollment and supported tender rules. Historical purchases do not earn retroactively merely because a customer later joins, and some liability or account-funded transactions have different treatment from eligible cash or card purchases.

faq.q: Are rewards a discount that changes the sale's tax calculation?
faq.a: In the supported redemption design, rewards pay an already-calculated total rather than rewriting line prices or tax treatment. Demonstrate the intended currency and tender combination so the store understands both the balance and payment requirements.

margin-and-seasonal-performance.intro: Strong sales do not always mean a strong season. Margin and seasonal performance bring recorded revenue together with explicitly reviewed cost, inventory and labour evidence, helping the owner ask more informed questions about categories, timing and the work that supported the result.
explanation: The quality of the evidence matters more than a confidently displayed percentage. Purchase cost is not automatically the cost of goods sold, and missing labour or average inventory should not be treated as zero. The supported reporting distinguishes available information from a result that still lacks the inputs needed for a meaningful calculation.

Use the view as a disciplined review tool. Comparing periods or product groups can help direct a buying or staffing conversation, but it does not forecast demand or guarantee profit. Preserve source and correction context so a revised figure can be understood rather than appearing to change without explanation.

capabilities.title: Reviewed margin
capabilities.text: Consider net revenue alongside appropriate reviewed cost-of-goods-sold evidence, making the calculation's business meaning clearer than subtracting an arbitrary supplier receipt cost from a sales total.

capabilities.title: Seasonal context
capabilities.text: Review the supported period and category information with its relevant scope, giving the owner a basis for discussing changing performance rather than relying on one all-time revenue number.

capabilities.title: Honest missing inputs
capabilities.text: Keep unavailable cost, labour or inventory evidence distinguishable from zero, so the report does not present an apparently complete profitability measure when a required component has not been established.

faq.q: Will the POS calculate accurate profit just from purchase prices?
faq.a: Not by assumption. Reviewed cost of goods sold, returns, inventory and other relevant evidence have their own requirements. Recorded receipt costs can help the review without becoming a substitute for the actual supported cost basis.

faq.q: What if our labour or average inventory information is missing?
faq.a: The result should remain unavailable where the calculation requires that input. Treating missing evidence as zero can produce a misleading ratio, so establish and review the source before using the figure to make a business decision.

supplier-shortages-and-backorders.intro: A short delivery leaves two jobs: record what arrived and decide what happens to the remainder. Supplier shortages and backorders keep that unfinished commitment visible, helping the buyer follow up without turning undelivered plants into stock the store never actually received.
explanation: The original order still provides context after a partial shipment. Staff need to understand which quantities remain outstanding, whether the supplier expects another delivery and whether the store should retain or cancel the remainder. Keeping that work connected is clearer than closing the whole order or creating another unrelated one.

Changes should preserve completed receiving evidence. A remainder cancellation must not erase the accepted plants, costs and earlier exceptions. If a substitute is offered, verify its actual identity and terms before recording it through receiving rather than relabelling a requested item to make the order look complete.

capabilities.title: Outstanding quantities
capabilities.text: Review the order remainder separately from accepted receipts, giving the buyer a clearer view of what is still owed rather than treating the first delivery as completion of every line.

capabilities.title: Supplier follow-up
capabilities.text: Keep the shortage and backorder conversation tied to the original commitment, helping staff decide which remaining goods still need confirmation and which part of the arrangement has changed.

capabilities.title: Preserved receipts
capabilities.text: Retain the quantities and cost evidence already recorded when resolving the remainder, so a cancellation or later delivery cannot quietly rewrite the history of plants previously accepted by the store.

faq.q: Does leaving an item on backorder add it to available stock?
faq.a: No. An outstanding supplier commitment is different from a confirmed receipt. Staff must record the actual arrival through receiving before treating undelivered plants as stock physically available for customer sale or fulfilment.

faq.q: Can we cancel only the part the supplier cannot deliver?
faq.a: The supported remainder workflow reviews the exact outstanding quantity while preserving earlier receipts. Confirm the supplier arrangement and authorized decision, then resolve the unfulfilled portion without deleting the goods and costs already recorded.
